replacements.original: Reflection gives the other orientation with $q$ replaced by $q^{-1}$, contributing $q^{-s}\delta-q^{-s+1}=q^{-s-1}$ for $s\ge1$ and $\delta-q=q^{-1}$ for $s=0$.
replacements.proposed: For the second branch, first choose the cap-cup term $-v^{-1}d_i$ rather than the through term $v1$ at the outer crossing of $g_i=v1-v^{-1}d_i$. For $s\ge1$, propagate this branch along the defect strings using the same cap-slide identities above: at each of the first $s-1$ defect positions, the surviving pair of smoothing coefficients is $(-v^{-1})(-v^{-1})=q^{-1}$; each alternative connects two defects and is zero in the link-state quotient. At the last crossing, the through smoothing contributes $v$ and the smoothing closing the remaining loop contributes $-v^{-1}\delta$. Including the initial coefficient, this branch therefore contributes $(-v^{-1})q^{-(s-1)}(v-v^{-1}\delta)=q^{-s}\delta-q^{-s+1}=q^{-s-1}$. For $s=0$, no defect string intervenes: the two terminal resolutions give $\delta-q=q^{-1}$. The surviving matchings in this second branch are reflected versions of the first branch's matchings, but the coefficients just computed come from its own smoothing choices; reflection is linear and does not invert the scalar $q$.

original_native_finding.concern: Step 7.1 says, “Reflection gives the other orientation with q replaced by q^{-1}”. The defined diagram reflection is linear and fixes scalars, so reflection alone does not justify that substitution. The second smoothing branch and its coefficients need to be identified explicitly. The cited Ridout–Saint-Aubin Appendix A, Proposition A.2, equations (A.9)–(A.11), https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.4505, derives this contribution by expanding the second branch before comparing reflected diagrams. That argument supports the claimed eigenvalue and splitting condition; the local explanation omits this distinction.
